title: Prompt Archipelago: Explorations & Seed Notes
content:
Overview:
This is a personal scratchpad for an exploratory prompt library approach I started calling the 'archipelago' model: small, independent prompt clusters (islands) that can be combined via lightweight adapters (boats). Goal is to make few-shot sets modular and recombinable to reduce brittle full-template rewrites when surface changes occur.

Quick motivation / tradeoffs:
- Problem: monolithic prompt templates get fragile as product copy/requirements drift. Small changes break many few-shot exemplars.
- Archipelago idea: treat exemplars as island-level assets grouped by intent, style, and failure-profile. Compose islands at runtime rather than editing a single giant template.
- Tradeoff: increases routing/selection complexity; but reduces per-change maintenance and supports targeted A/B of islands.

Hypotheses to test:
1) Short, intent-focused exemplars (3–5 lines) are more robust to domain copy drift than narrative exemplars (3–4 sentence examples).
2) Metric-stable islands: some islands produce lower variance in quality across prompts/tasks — these are candidate 'base islands' to always include.
3) Island ensembles with simple scoring (n-gram overlap + logprob heuristics) outperform static monolith when token budget <= 120 tokens exemplar budget.

Seed island taxonomy (initial):
- persona-basic: direct role + constraints (tone, length) — very small (1–2 lines).
- persona-rich: role w/ short backstory + example output (3–4 lines).
- instruction-strict: lots of guardrails, explicit "do not" rules.
- instruction-loose: high-level goals, allow creativity.
- format-examples: explicit desired JSON/table templates.
- error-example: shows a bad answer and correction pattern (for self-critique).
- retrieval-anchor: contains a short provenance line reference for when model must cite.

Example island exemplar (persona-basic):
"You are an assistant that answers concisely in bullet points. Keep each bullet <= 20 words. No speculation."

Example island exemplar (format-examples):
"Output as JSON: {\"summary\": <one-line>, \"actions\": [<short actions>]}"

Few-shot pool building notes:
- Pool size: start with 12 islands, 1 exemplar each. Compose 3–4 islands per request.
- Selection heuristics: match intent tags (intent, tone, format), then apply frequency smoothing (prefer smaller islands when token budget low).
- Few-shot exemplars should avoid repeating exact product copy; instead use abstracted placeholders (e.g., <product_feature>) to reduce brittleness.

Failure cases observed (manual logging during prototype runs):
- Case A: ensemble with persona-rich + instruction-loose => hallucination of product features (model adds fake endpoints).
  - Mitigation: prefer instruction-strict island when user question mentions "API" or "integration".
- Case B: format-examples conflicting with persona-basic (bulleted terse vs JSON) => model chooses one and ignores other.
  - Mitigation: add small arbitration island: "When multiple format instructions conflict, prioritize the format-examples island."
- Case C: few-shot exemplars with rhetorical questions cause style bleed (assistant responds with questions).
  - Mitigation: rewrite exemplar to declarative outputs.

Experiment plan (short):
- Phase 0: offline slicing of our existing prompt bench (RWD-PROMPT-BENCH v1) to produce island candidates. Compute token lengths, lexical overlap matrices. (Jupyter notebooks: prompt-archipelago-eda.ipynb)
- Phase 1: small online A/B on internal QA harness (1000 queries): compare monolith baseline vs archipelago compose-3 ensemble. Metrics: accept-rate (binary), avg token cost, regression rate on safety tests.
- Phase 2: add adapter scoring using short LM-scoring step (logprob on exemplar outputs) vs cheap heuristics. Measure latency delta.

Evaluation notes / metrics to capture:
- Quality: binary accept + human-rated 1–5 usefulness. Need 200 human evals per arm to have signal.
- Stability: variance in human score across small edit (swap phrase in product copy).
- Cost: median token spend per request (include selection overhead).
- Latency: median additional ms for selection step; goal <= 35ms added on hosted infra.
- Regression surfaces: monitor hallucination flags (manual + regex heuristics).

Prompt templates to try (scaffolded):
1) Compose template skeleton:
"System: {{island:persona-basic}} {{island:instruction-strict}}\nUser: {{user_question}}\nAssistant:"

2) Adapter arbitration island (short):
"If the islands above conflict, apply this priority order: format-examples > instruction-strict > persona-rich > persona-basic."

Quick heuristics for island selection function (pseudocode sketch):
- intent_tags = extract_intent(user_question)
- candidate_islands = islands.filter(i => i.tags intersect intent_tags)
- if token_budget < 120 => favor islands with size <= 40 tokens
- if user_question includes keywords ["api","endpoint","auth"] => ensure instruction-strict present

Tests to write (tickets):
- create prompt-archipelago unit tests for selection logic (Jest): PR suggested https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-lab/pull/278
- add mimic queries to eval harness: JIRA-RWD-981

Loose notes / TODOs (brain dump):
- Try hybrid: keep 1 monolith exemplar + 2 islands — see if that reduces arbitration failures.
- Tokenization sanity: verify islands tokenized independently produce expected counts across models (gpt-2 vs opt vs local quantized).
- Safety island? Create an island that encodes safety filters as soft constraints (likely via explicit refusal examples). Could be included always for public-facing endpoints.
- UX: console view showing which islands were included for a request (helps debugging). Hook to Redwood Console per-request metadata.

Questions to answer in next session:
- How to version islands? semantic hash of exemplar text or tag-based? Need roll-forward/rollback plan for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Runtime cost: can we cache selected island compositions per-route and TTL them? Warm cache invalidation policy?

References & snippets:
- small local eval script: ./scripts/archipelago_eval.sh (needs to be pushed)
- local notebook: notebooks/prompt-archipelago-experiments.ipynb
- relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-lab/pull/278

Scratch: few-shot example set (3 islands combined) — direct trial candidate:
System: You are an assistant that answers concisely in bullet points. Keep each bullet <= 20 words. No speculation.
System: Provide output as JSON: {"summary": <one-line>, "actions": [<short actions>]}
User: "How do I integrate Redwood SDK into an existing Node service? Provide steps and quick caveats."
Expected assistant: JSON with summary and 3 short action steps. No speculative URLs.

Personal notes:
- Keep this document lightweight. Move matured patterns to shared_confluence page (CONFLUENCE-PRM-4412) once we have reproducible eval gains.
- Save example islands to small flat file store (islands/*.json) with metadata: tags, token_count, last_used.

Next short-term actions (this week):
- Pull 50 candidate exemplars from prompt-bench, chunk into islands. (owner: Maya)
- Wire simple selection heuristic into eval harness and run A/B on 1k queries (owner: Ethan)
- Draft Confluence intro doc and plan for console view (owner: Sofia)

End of scratchpad — will iterate.
